Steps now fill the space as a row-major multi-column grid, modeled on standard TUI grid pickers. Research (ratatui docs, tui-widget-list, popular apps) pointed to row-major cells with directional navigation as the common pattern. Implementation: EditorState gains steps_columns (default 1, so all existing single-column tests/goldens stay byte-identical); the run loop derives columns each frame from terminal width via steps_columns_for_width (cell = widest filtered step + 9, clamped 1..=6) and App::set_steps_columns stores it. window_bounds is replaced by grid_window(index, len, columns, rows, scroll) which scrolls by one grid row and keeps pages column-aligned; steps_window/realign use it. Navigation: Up/Down/j/k move by columns (row stride), Left/Right/h/l move by one cell wrapping across rows; rendering lays cells left-to-right with row-local column padding and the cursor marker on the focused cell. The run log is now written to disk line by line: the stdout/stderr pump threads replace io::copy+BufWriter (flushed only at end-of-stream) with a pump_lines() read_until(newline) loop that writes and flushes the file after every line (terminal tee unchanged). This unblocks real-time tailing of a running profile — the TUI follow view polls the file every tick and now sees output as it happens instead of only after the run ends. Test: run_log_flushes_after_each_line uses a FlushCounter writer to prove exactly one flush per line plus complete content. just check green (229 lib tests).

Every column of the steps grid now lines up across rows: body_lines builds the whole cell matrix first, computes per-column widths (max cell width across all rendered rows), and pads each cell to its own column's width with the 2-space gap — instead of the previous row-local padding that let column boundaries drift whenever step names differed in length (only the first column looked aligned). Partial last-row cells render short. Test: multi_column_grid_aligns_every_column_across_rows uses ragged name lengths and asserts columns 2 and 3 start at identical offsets on both rendered rows. just check green (230 lib tests).

Run now opens the live log view immediately: run_now() sets View::Logs(LogsState::follow) at keypress instead of waiting for systemctl start to return, so the user lands on the log screen right away and x (stop) is reachable for the whole run — including while the start job is still in flight (systemd serializes the concurrent stop). pending_follow and run_after_result are deleted; the follow header now shows the real transitions (brief 'starting' while the start job runs -> 'running · elapsed' -> 'finished ok'/'FAILED'), and the footer spinner keeps the 'starting {name}' label honest. On start failure the error message shows and the log view header reports not-running. Tests: run_now_shows_loading_then_starts_the_service_through_the_manager now asserts the view opens before settle, and live_view_x_works_while_the_start_is_still_in_flight proves the stop reaches systemd mid-start. just check green (231 lib tests).

A) An engaged (committed) filter stays visible: the footer shows ' /query' and the steps header ' filter: query' while is_engaged() — the ▏ caret appears only while typing — and active_filter() is scoped per view so a dashboard filter no longer leaks into the editor footer. C) Single post-edit policy: both surfaces CLAMP the selection to the surviving rows (editor previously hard-reset index/scroll to 0; Esc-clear also clamps instead of resetting) — grid_window tolerates any index. E) One FilterState::filter_query() helper (query + ▏ while editing) feeds the footer, the steps header, and the 'Profiles (filter: …)' title, so the three formats stop drifting. The filter footer hint now also shows while typing in the editor steps filter. Tests: active_filter_reports_dashboard_and_editor_steps_queries extended (caret, committed persistence, no leak), steps_header test extended (committed without caret), dashboard_arrows_move_the_selection_while_typing_a_filter, narrowing_the_steps_filter_clamps_instead_of_resetting. just check green (235 lib tests).

The filterable-list key dance now lives in one place: input::handle_filter_typing(filter, key, &mut index, len, stride) routes Up (saturating sub) / Down (clamp to last surviving row) to the index and everything else to the filter, with stride 1 for the linear dashboard list and steps_columns for the grid; both call sites then run their own clamp/realign (clamp_selection / clamp_steps_selection). FilterState::clear_query() replaces the two hand-rolled query resets. Pure structural refactor: all 235 pre-existing tests stayed green untouched (the acceptance bar), plus a unit suite for the component (filter_typing_navigates_with_the_list_stride, filter_typing_edits_the_query_for_everything_else, clear_query_drops_the_match_and_leaves_edit_mode). just check green (238 lib tests).

Umbrella closed via the user-approved refinement split: topmatic-vq0 (UX consistency — committed filter stays visible with caret-only-while-typing, arrows move the selection mid-query on both surfaces, single clamp policy, one filter_query chip helper for footer/header/title, per-view scoping) and topmatic-uoi (structural — handle_filter_typing + clear_query extracted so the dance cannot drift again). Schedule/options keep plain row selection: they have no filter today, so there was nothing to unify there. Commits a756a13 + this one; just check green (238 lib tests).

Run now shows a true 'running' state instead of lingering in 'starting'. Two host-verified root causes fixed: (1) the service is Type=oneshot so plain 'systemctl start' blocked for the whole run (measured 11.1s for a 10.2s run, keeping the footer 'starting {name}' spinner alive the entire time) — start_service now passes --no-block (verified returning instantly on host); (2) during the whole execution the unit sits in SubState 'activating' where 'systemctl is-active' exits rc=3, so service_active() was false for the entire run and the follow header never showed 'running' — detection now uses 'systemctl show -p ActiveState --value' via active_state_means_running (active|activating), and service_since reads ExecMainStartTimestamp (ActiveEnterTimestamp stays empty until a oneshot finishes — host-verified fixture), giving an honest elapsed timer. pty-driver acceptance on host: r+1s header 'running all-daily', output streaming mid-run, 'finished ok' at r+10s, no 'starting' spinner. Trade-off accepted: with --no-block a queued-but-failing start no longer errors the job; the failure surfaces via the status file as with timer-fired runs. Unit test: activating_counts_as_running_for_oneshot_services. just check green (239 lib tests); binaries deployed.

Runs are no longer reported as failures they did not have. Three display lies fixed: (1) pressing r on an already-running profile is absorbed in the TUI — it logs '{name} already running' and jumps straight to the live view without issuing a second start (with --no-block systemd would merge the job, but the old path produced lock-skip outcomes: 7 rapid host runs 19:16-19:29 wrote skipped statuses); (2) a skipped outcome renders as '{profile} skipped — a run was already active' instead of 'FAILED (exit None)' in the follow header; (3) a status file older than the current run's start (running_since via ExecMainStartTimestamp) shows 'not running' instead of posing as the run's result — covers runs killed before writing status. The live log now auto-scrolls: LogsState tracks a follow_offset counting LINES FROM THE BOTTOM (0 = pinned), replacing the old scroll-from-top on content that was wholesale-replaced every tick (it drifted and showed stale positions). Up/k scroll back one line, Down/j scrolls forward, and reaching the bottom (offset back to 0) re-engages auto-follow so new output keeps arriving at the visible edge. Render computes from_top = total_lines - visible_height - follow_offset using the panel area, so the newest line is always visible while pinned no matter how the tail grows. Footer hint gains '↑↓ scroll'. Log scrolling fixed end to end. (1) Held-key lag: the event loop consumed ONE event per iteration, so autorepeat queued faster than the 200ms cadence and scrolling kept going after release — the loop now drains every immediately-available event in an inner poll(0) batch (each handled, one tick/draw after the batch), verified on host with a 30-event PgUp/Up burst: no runaway frames, post-release quiet, esc responsive. (2) PageUp/PageDown/Home/End work in BOTH log views: follow keeps its lines-from-bottom offset (PageUp +page, PageDown -page, Home jumps to content top, End re-pins at 0) and the browse view scrolls from the top (Home=0, End=last line, pages clamped by content length; list mode pages entries); the page size comes from a Cell<viewport> recorded at render time, following the existing list_area pattern so key handling needs no area. (3) The stray vertical 'A' column: run logs contain raw ANSI (host fixture 20260906-233646: ESC[2K, ESC[32m, ESC[1m, ESC[m, CR) which ratatui rendered as garbage glyphs — sanitize_log_text strips CSI/OSC sequences, CR/backspace/del and expands tabs before ANY display path (tail() and load_selected/set_content), keeping printable unicode intact. Refactor license from the user: kept the change surgical (set_content centralizes content+line count; Cell viewport), no deeper rewrite needed. Ctrl+C now kills the app from anywhere, with a clean terminal — and the analysis the user asked for: a literal native SIGINT kill is NOT cleanly possible for a raw-mode TUI (ratatui::init disables ISIG so the kernel never generates SIGINT — Ctrl+C arrives as a key event; and a default-disposition signal death would skip teardown, leaving the alternate screen on and mouse capture enabled — a corrupted terminal, which is why every mainstream TUI treats Ctrl+C as a graceful exit). Implemented the user's pre-approved fallback: Ctrl+C (Char c/C + CONTROL) sets should_quit at the very top of handle_key, BEFORE the overlay/filter dispatches, so it kills even while a filter is active or a popup is open — strictly stronger than q, which respects input state. q and Ctrl+C share the same immediate graceful path (loop break -> ratatui::restore), so 'q works like the kill' is satisfied: identical behavior, cross-platform by construction (key event, works on macOS too). Host-verified via pty: Ctrl+C mid-filter exits AND the teardown emits alt-screen-leave + mouse-capture-off. No legend added, as requested. Tests: ctrl_c_quits_from_anywhere_including_active_filters (dashboard filter + editor), plain_c_without_control_types_normally. just check green (247 lib tests); binaries deployed.
